chapters.title: Chapter 1: Hardening Authentication Middleware
chapters.content:
## JWT Authentication & Expiration Verification

This chapter documents the practical implementation of algorithm validation and token expiration checks to prevent algorithm confusion attacks and expired token replays.

### The Security Diff
```go
// Check token expiration
if time.Now().After(claims["exp"]) {
    http.Error(w, "Token expired", http.StatusUnauthorized)
    return
}
```

### Verification Steps
1. Run `rg -n "jwt.ValidateToken" .` across the repo.
2. Apply the surgical patch.
3. Execute unit tests.

To start an LLM (Large Language Model) on your local laptop using the llmctl command, follow these steps:

1. Ensure llmctl is installed: If llmctl is not already installed on your system, you will need to install it first. You can typically install it via a package manager or by downloading it from the official source.

2. Configure llmctl: Before starting the LLM, you need to configure llmctl with the necessary settings. This usually involves setting up API keys, specifying the model, and configuring any other required parameters.

3. Start the LLM: Once llmctl is configured, you can start the LLM by running the following command in your terminal:
